summary: The milestone completed 12 compute-bound experiments in 18.0 minutes. The 6.99-minute randomized-label learning audit and 4.2-minute adapter-withheld ARC callback run were the longest; no data available this milestone identifies their costly phases.
bottlenecks_identified: The randomized-label learning audit formed the critical path, followed by the adapter-withheld ARC callback run; no data available this milestone explains which internal phases consumed their time.
Accelerator telemetry consists of a closing snapshot rather than task-aligned samples, so compute-window utilization efficiency cannot be established.
Launch receipts do not state concurrent model count or runner selection, so no data available this milestone establishes whether any task qualified for DualGPURunner or missed it.
improvements_suggested: Emit a task-scoped execution receipt that joins phase timing, GPU utilization, memory allocation, process identity, and device assignment.
Record concurrent model count and runner selection at launch, invoking DualGPURunner only for workloads that load two or more models in parallel.
Add a capacity-aware scheduler that reclaims inactive model processes and places eligible independent work on the available second GPU.
Instrument checkpoints around the randomized-label learning audit and adapter-withheld ARC callback path before attempting code-level optimization.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Join phase and accelerator samples to each experiment in one execution receipt.
Capture model-count and runner-dispatch evidence for every compute launch.
Schedule eligible independent workloads across both GPUs after verifying ownership and reclaiming inactive allocations.
meta_reflection: The reconstructed timing is sufficient to rank the critical path but not to explain it. No data available this milestone supports a measured savings forecast, a task-window GPU-efficiency verdict, or a parallel-model runner-failure claim.
